question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the curb and look to determine if the emergency vehicle is on your street.,b:Keep driving until you clearly see the vehicle.,c:Slow down but do not stop until you identify its location.
note: If you hear a close siren but are unsure of its location, safely pull over to the right and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

question: When stopped by an officer for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:The driver's license.,b:Only proof of insurance.,c:Only proof of registration.
note: When stopped, the driver is required to provide their driver license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance.

question: When may you text while driving in North Carolina?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you can text without looking at your phone.,c:If you use voice-to-text and never look at the device.
note: Texting while driving is prohibited in North Carolina because it is a major distraction to the vehicle operator.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow signal for a lane mean?
options: a:Traffic in that lane must turn in the direction of the arrow and has the right-of-way.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green but you may go straight or turn.,c:It means proceed only if accompanied by a circular green light.
note: A green arrow indicates that traffic in the lane may proceed in the arrow's direction and oncoming traffic must stop for turning traffic.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal and constitutes driving under the influence.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow mean on a traffic signal?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,b:It means drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow without yielding.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow signals that a red arrow is imminent; slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, when must you pull over and stop?
options: a:Regardless of its direction — pull to the right and stop.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull to the right and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren regardless of whether it is ahead of you or behind you.

question: A two-lane road with a broken yellow centerline tells you what about traffic direction?
options: a:Vehicles on the other side travel the opposite direction (two-way road).,b:The road is one way.,c:The road is under construction.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates passing is permitted when safe.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and then driving?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you had only one drink.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious safety problem; alcohol impairs judgment and driving ability.

question: How should you consider railroad crossings in terms of safety?
options: a:Dangerous — always look and listen before crossing.,b:Generally safe because trains are infrequent.,c:Safe places to stop and park.
note: Railroad crossings can be hazardous; always look and listen for trains, obey signals, and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What traffic signal requires you to come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal functions the same as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, then proceed when the way is clear.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.,b:At the approaching vehicle’s headlights.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by high-beam headlights of an approaching vehicle.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift into neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes, then pull off the road when safe.,b:Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up by hand.,c:Shift the transmission into park while driving to stop quickly.
note: If the throttle sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, brake steadily, exit traffic when safe, and turn off the engine.

question: How often should drivers check their mirrors under normal conditions?
options: a:About every 10 seconds.,b:About every 30 seconds.,c:About every 15 seconds.
note: Check mirrors roughly every 8–15 seconds (about every 10 seconds) to monitor vehicles around you without taking your eyes off the road for more than an instant.

question: When a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway, what should drivers do?
options: a:May continue driving.,b:Must stop until the bus moves.,c:Must stop until the stop arm is retracted.
note: If the highway is divided by a median, drivers on the opposite side may continue; on undivided highways both directions must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic signal turns from green to yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Brake sharply to stop immediately in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow indicates the light will soon be red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise continue through the intersection.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check the area.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine so children hear you moving.
note: Always get out and check behind your vehicle when children are present rather than relying only on mirrors or cameras.

question: Approximately what percentage of highway fatalities involve alcohol?
options: a:About 38 percent.,b:About 10 percent.,c:About 25 percent.
note: Roughly 38% of highway fatalities involve alcohol-impaired drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make driving less than perfect.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when traffic is heavy.
note: Posted limits are for ideal conditions; reduce speed when visibility, traction, or other conditions are impaired.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important in winter.
note: You should not use cruise control in snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions; winter driving requires extra caution and preparation.

question: If you accumulate seven points on your driving record, which outcome is correct?
options: a:I only (required to file proof of financial responsibility),b:II only (you can have three points deducted by completing a driver improvement clinic),c:Both I & II
note: Accumulating seven points can result in assignment to a driver improvement clinic; upon satisfactory completion, three points may be deducted from your record.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a good rule to remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to improve visibility.
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with traffic flow, obey speed limits, and only pass when necessary and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in cities and towns is:
options: a:35 mph.,b:10 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless posted otherwise, the default speed limit in cities and towns is 35 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the nearest point before the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:Only after slowing to verify that cross traffic is clear.,c:Only if you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if that means entering the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest to the intersecting roadway where you have a view of approaching traffic; do not enter the intersection to obtain a better view.

question: What do orange traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zone warnings.,b:School zone warnings.,c:Regulatory instructions.
note: Orange diamond-shaped signs with black symbols or letters are typically used to warn drivers of highway work zones and other temporary traffic conditions.

question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
options: a:Communicate your intentions to other road users by signaling and using lights or horn appropriately.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane.,c:Drive exclusively on side streets to avoid traffic.
note: Communicate with other drivers and road users by signaling and using lights or the horn when necessary to reduce unexpected actions.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing.,b:Start moving as soon as the visible train passes.,c:Cross immediately after the first train has passed.
note: Do not start across until you have a clear view down all tracks; another train could be approaching on a separate track.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The driver must yield.,b:The pedestrian must yield.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should never attempt to pass another vehicle when:
options: a:On a hill or curve where visibility is limited.,b:You are traveling below the speed limit.,c:Traffic is light.
note: Never pass where your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, before or on railroad crossings, or where marked no-passing zones exist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which situations?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only when a police officer signals you to stop.
note: You must stop at intersections with stop signs, at solid or flashing red lights, or whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: Which of the following statements about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered crossing gates.,b:You do not have to stop when directed by a flagger.,c:All railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
note: Do not go around lowered gates; stop when directed by flaggers or warning devices. Not all crossings have gates or signals.

question: When roads may be slippery, you should:
options: a:Reduce your following distance and avoid sudden speed or steering changes.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: On slippery roads reduce speed and following distance and avoid sudden inputs; do not use cruise control.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what should you do before you start?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance and review directions or a map.,b:Rely solely on roadside signs to find your way.,c:Drive without detailed plans and figure it out as you go.
note: Plan the route in advance rather than relying only on a vague idea or roadside signs.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Continue through the intersection at normal speed.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution: slow down, look, and proceed with care.

question: Which factors greatly affect your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:Road conditions, vehicle brakes and tires, and your reaction time.,b:The time of day only.,c:Signal lights only.
note: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, vehicle condition (brakes, tires), road conditions, and speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue without stopping.
note: At an open intersection, yield to a vehicle that arrived on your right; that vehicle has the right-of-way.

question: What is the meaning of a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection?
options: a:Yield — slow down and give right-of-way as required.,b:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,c:Slow only if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign means yield: reduce speed and yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does it indicate?
options: a:The road ahead will become narrower.,b:You are approaching a construction area.,c:There is an intersection ahead.
note: An edge line that angles toward the center indicates the roadway width decreases ahead; use caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles with the right-of-way.,b:Maintain normal speed without checking for pedestrians.,c:Stop completely regardless of conditions.
note: Unless a sign prohibits the turn, you may turn on green but must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the traffic light is working, which should you follow?
options: a:The traffic light only.,b:The officer's directions.,c:Your own judgment rather than either.
note: When an officer is directing traffic, their signals take precedence over traffic lights and signs; follow the officer's directions.

question: How should you respond when approaching a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Stop if it is safe to do so; otherwise proceed through the intersection.,b:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,c:Accelerate because you have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will turn red soon; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed through the intersection cautiously.

question: What can happen if a bicyclist does not obey traffic laws?
options: a:They can be ticketed.,b:They are exempt from traffic laws.,c:They will always receive only a warning.
note: Bicyclists have the same responsibilities as drivers and can be cited for traffic violations.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Ignore the guard and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized.
note: Always obey crossing guards and use extra caution in school zones to protect children.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you want to enter is a:
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe; solid lines prohibit crossing.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower to become sober.
note: Only time allows the body to reduce BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower BAC.

question: If your car begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Keep the front wheels straight.,c:Steer in the opposite direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go and correct as it begins to straighten.

question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained and maintain safe speed in wet conditions.,b:Use cruise control at all times.,c:Drive faster to get through standing water quickly.
note: Maintain good tire tread and proper inflation, and reduce speed on wet roads to reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: When backing your vehicle, what is the recommended practice?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door to check behind you.
note: Before backing, check behind the vehicle. Turn your head to look through the rear window and do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: A regulatory sign that has a red circle with a slash through a black symbol indicates what?
options: a:The specified action is forbidden.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means the action shown is prohibited (for example, no U-turn).

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do next?
options: a:Watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road before proceeding.,b:Proceed as soon as the bus driver looks at you.,c:Accelerate quickly to get past the bus.
note: When a bus is unloading, children may be walking near the roadway; proceed only after ensuring it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit outside cities and towns unless otherwise posted?
options: a:55 mph.,b:45 mph.,c:35 mph.
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the default speed limit outside cities and towns is 55 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Both vehicles should make hand signals to communicate.
note: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected actions by other drivers.,b:It prevents other drivers from changing lanes.,c:It speeds up traffic flow.
note: Maintaining space around your vehicle ensures you have time to respond to mistakes by other road users.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:The same as a stop sign; come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,b:The same as a yield sign.,c:Slow down but do not stop.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and yielding to other traffic before proceeding.

question: What practice best ensures safety when you are about to back your vehicle?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check before you get into the driver's seat.,b:Check the rearview mirror from the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn just before reversing.
note: Because it is hard to see small children and objects behind a vehicle, walk around and inspect the area before you begin backing.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection, yielding as necessary.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down and watch for cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving much slower than the posted speed and are causing traffic to back up on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road at the first safe location to let other vehicles pass.,b:Refuse to let following cars pass you.,c:Continue driving at the same slow speed because you have the right-of-way.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving significantly below the speed of other vehicles, pull over safely and allow vehicles to pass.

question: Which driving adjustment is appropriate when the weather suddenly changes?
options: a:All of the above — adjust driving, slow down in rain/fog, and watch vehicles behind you.,b:Only slow down in rain and fog.,c:Ignore weather changes unless they’re severe.
note: Sudden weather changes require adapting your driving: slow down in rain and fog and be aware of traffic behind you that may not adjust.

question: At night, which road user is the hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared to signs or roadside objects, so exercise extra caution.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down until it passes, staying in your lane.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: You must immediately pull to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle using lights or siren until it has passed, unless directed otherwise.

question: What helps a person recover from the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,c:Drinking a strong cup of coffee.
note: Only time will allow the body to eliminate alcohol from the system; other remedies do not reduce impairment.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A steady yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light signals you to slow down and proceed with caution; a flashing red means stop.

question: What is the immediate administrative consequence of refusing a chemical test when an officer requests one?
options: a:Immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days and additional DMV action.,b:Only a short warning.,c:Automatic community service.
note: Refusal results in immediate license revocation for at least 30 days and further DMV penalties (often 12 months).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:Only on highways with three or more lanes.,c:Whenever traffic is light and visibility is good.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings where visibility is poor.

question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Give pedestrians the right-of-way.,b:Proceed because vehicles have priority.,c:Yield only if there are traffic signals present.
note: Pedestrians in a marked crosswalk have the right-of-way; drivers must stop and let them cross safely.

question: Which action most effectively avoids alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Say “No thanks, I'm driving” if someone offers you a drink.,c:Call a taxi after you have already had several drinks.
note: The only reliable way to avoid drunk driving is to decide not to drive before you start drinking; alcohol impairs judgment and decision-making.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
options: a:The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right yields to the driver on the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or traveling fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Cross at your own risk if there is no signal.
note: Look and listen before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close enough to pose danger, you must wait.

question: How often must a vehicle pass a safety inspection in North Carolina?
options: a:Once a year.,b:Twice a year.,c:Every six months.
note: Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (and emissions in certain counties) prior to registration renewal.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching you?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,b:Continue driving and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping when safe to do so.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Traffic is moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Traffic in both lanes moves the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Drivers may never pass in either direction.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and permits passing when safe and clear of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers be doing?
options: a:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and yield when necessary.,b:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Signal only after beginning the turn.
note: Signal three to five seconds before the turn, check mirrors, move into the left lane if appropriate, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get off at the next exit and circle back safely.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,c:Back up in your lane to reach the missed exit.
note: Do not back up on the highway. Proceed to the next exit, then re-enter the highway to return to your missed exit.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle; it warns that the vehicle is likely moving at 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop and yield appropriately.,b:Park as far off the road as possible and wait for power to return.,c:Turn on hazard lights and proceed without stopping.
note: When signals are out you should yield as at a four-way stop and proceed in turn when it is safe.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog. Reduce speed and watch for taillights of vehicles ahead.

question: If you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, how should you react?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Stop immediately in your lane wherever you are.,c:Proceed slowly and let the emergency vehicle maneuver around you.
note: On two-lane or undivided roads, pull as far to the right as possible and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign usually indicate?
options: a:Warning — conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directions to cities and towns ahead.,c:Traffic laws and regulations you must follow.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions such as curves, intersections, or changes in the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which actions should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Signal only and then change lanes quickly.,c:Check mirrors only because they show everything you need.
note: Before changing lanes, signal your intentions, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear.

question: Drinking coffee after alcohol will:
options: a:Not reduce your blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancel the effects of alcohol.,c:Reduce your blood alcohol concentration quickly.
note: Drinking coffee may help you feel more awake but it does not change your blood alcohol concentration or speed sobering.

question: When passing an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road, drivers should:
options: a:Vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle or slow down if unable to move over.,b:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.,c:Stop and offer assistance unless instructed otherwise.
note: You must move over a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle; if not safe to do so, slow down.

question: In urban areas, approximately how many people killed in traffic accidents are pedestrians?
options: a:Two out of every five.,b:One out of every six.,c:Five out of every eight.
note: In urban areas, about two in every five people killed in traffic accidents are pedestrians; be extra cautious near them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe or illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a curve in the roadway.,b:On a wide, straight highway.,c:Where there is a separate turning lane.
note: Do not pass on curves, hills, at intersections, or near railroad crossings where visibility is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield.,b:Either one can go first.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield.
note: When two vehicles enter an intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Its effect depends on the amount consumed, not the type of beverage.,b:It affects reflexes less if you drink beer instead of wine.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you most.
note: The effect of alcohol on reflexes and judgment depends on how much alcohol enters the bloodstream, not the specific type of beverage consumed.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an approaching railroad crossing and to use extra caution.

question: You may be required to attend a driver improvement clinic if you accumulate how many points?
options: a:Seven points.,b:Three points.,c:One point.
note: Accumulating seven points may require you to attend a driver improvement clinic; completing it can remove points from your record.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Fail to check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic.,b:Use a turn signal to indicate your intention.,c:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes without checking mirrors and blind spots; always signal and ensure the lane is clear.

question: What does a crossbuck sign identify?
options: a:Railroad crossing.,b:No passing zone.,c:School zone.
note: A crossbuck marks a railroad crossing; motorists must yield to trains and never try to beat a train across the tracks.

question: If a vehicle with ABS begins to lose traction on a slippery road, drivers should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal to accelerate out of the skid.
note: If your vehicle has an anti-lock braking system, press and hold the brake pedal hard. The ABS will automatically modulate braking to help maintain steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a:
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Gradually slow down and steer straight, then pull off the road.,b:Immediately apply hard braking to stop quickly.,c:Accelerate to maintain control.
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas, avoid hard braking, and gradually slow and steer to a safe area to stop.

question: If you find a defect that could affect safe operation of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible before driving.,c:Drive the vehicle more slowly until you can repair it.
note: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be repaired as soon as possible and before driving the vehicle if it creates a safety risk.

question: If a fire engine that is not using lights or siren is following you on a two-lane street, you should:
options: a:Continue to drive normally; you do not need to clear the way.,b:Stop immediately as quickly as possible.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If the emergency vehicle is not using lights or siren, you do not need to clear a path; continue driving normally.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals and warnings.,b:Share the right-of-way with trains and proceed when you feel like it.,c:Drive around lowered crossing gates if you are in a hurry.
note: Always obey lights, gates, and signs at light rail crossings and look both ways before crossing tracks; never go around lowered gates.

question: If a pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and be prepared to stop especially where children are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed carefully through an intersection displaying a yellow signal?
options: a:If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.,b:If a pedestrian is crossing the intersection.,c:If an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: If the light turns yellow while you are already within the intersection, continue through carefully and clear the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving slower than 45 mph, how far in advance should you signal before turning?
options: a:100 feet before the turn.,b:50 feet before the turn.,c:20 feet before the turn.
note: At speeds under 45 mph, signal at least 100 feet before you make a turn to alert other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using its siren or lights approaches, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but remain moving.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and maintain speed.
note: You must pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move right. What sequence should you use before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.,c:Signal and move immediately to the right without checking.
note: When moving right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over the right shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: How should a lap belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Buckle snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,b:Fit loosely so you can breathe easily.,c:Be hidden beneath the seat cushion.
note: Lap belts should lie low across the hip bones and shoulder belts should rest comfortably across the chest to provide proper restraint.

question: When the driver behind you signals a desire to pass, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Slow down to create a gap in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely.,c:Maintain your current speed and position.
note: Slow down or move right when safe to provide space for the other driver to complete the pass quickly and safely.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, then change lanes when safe.,b:Sound your horn to warn other drivers.,c:Turn on your headlights to indicate your lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, signal, and change lanes only when it is safe.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No, you may not.,b:Yes, it is allowed.,c:If there is no oncoming traffic, you may.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate no passing from either direction, except to turn into or out of a driveway or business.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
options: a:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,b:Use high beam headlights to better see ahead.,c:Speed up to get through the fog faster.
note: In fog you should slow down, drive cautiously, avoid high beams (which reduce visibility in fog), and use low beams to improve vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers while entering a street?
options: a:When entering from a garage, driveway, or alley.,b:When your traffic signal displays a green arrow.,c:When you are on the road to their left at an unmarked intersection.
note: You must yield to traffic on the public road when entering from a garage, driveway, or alley and yield to pedestrians on sidewalks.

question: Which practices help prevent accidents on long trips?
options: a:Stop every couple of hours to rest and avoid medications that cause drowsiness.,b:Drive continuously without breaks to reach your destination faster.,c:Only drive at night when traffic is lighter.
note: To reduce fatigue-related crashes, stop regularly to rest, avoid drowsy medications, and limit daily driving distance.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Wind gusts that may change your direction.,b:Loud engine noise only.,c:Excess air pollution but no steering effects.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts that may affect smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering.

question: What combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:An airbag alone.,c:A lap belt alone.
note: Seat belts greatly improve survival and injury prevention; airbags provide additional protection when used with seat belts.

question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:You may cross it to make a turn into a driveway or side road.,b:You may cross it during daylight hours only.,c:You may cross it to pass slower traffic.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing, but you may cross a solid yellow to make a permitted turn into a driveway or side road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you approach a yield sign at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway.,b:Always come to a complete stop before entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on your right.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and yield to cross traffic or pedestrians; stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously if you think most children are done.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, drivers must stop and not proceed until the stop arm is retracted and children are clear.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning.,b:Taking frequent rest stops during a long trip.,c:Getting too much sleep the night before driving.
note: Driving with fixed attention and not actively scanning the roadway can cause you to zone out and reduce alertness, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On narrow roads both drivers must allow adequate space for safe passage; you must allow at least half the main-traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Rely only on your mirrors to see vehicles beside you.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal in advance and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot. On freeways, signal about five seconds before changing lanes; in residential areas, signal about 100 feet ahead.

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
options: a:Low-beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,b:High-beam headlights to penetrate the fog.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in fog since high beams reflect off the fog and can reduce visibility further; use fog lights if your vehicle has them.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use an alternate route only.
note: On slippery roads, increase following distance and drive more slowly because it will take longer to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge when safe.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into a gap in traffic.
note: Drivers entering interstate traffic must yield to vehicles already on the highway and merge safely when an adequate gap exists.

question: To change lanes safely you should:
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, then change lanes when safe.,b:Check mirrors, then change lanes immediately after signaling.,c:Signal and rely only on mirrors when changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes activate your turn signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder in the direction of the move to check your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should the shared center lane be used on a multilane road with traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:For slowing or stopping to make a left turn.,b:As a passing lane.,c:As a through-traffic lane when traffic is slow.
note: The center two-way left-turn lane should be used only for preparing to make or executing a left turn; it is not a passing or through lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, start from the leftmost lane designated for left turns.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:Facing oncoming traffic.,b:With the flow of traffic.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, why should you allow a larger space cushion?
options: a:Because the vehicle ahead may roll back when starting again.,b:Because on hills you must always stop further behind.,c:Because intersections nearby require extra space.
note: On an uphill slope, allow extra space so the vehicle ahead can roll back slightly without causing a collision.

question: What is the most important rule about negotiating curves at speed?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part, then brake.,c:Accelerate before you enter the curve.
note: Because inertia pushes the vehicle outward in a curve, reduce your speed before you enter to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Immediately after you pass regardless of distance.,c:Only if you plan to turn left.
note: Return to the right lane after passing when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers.,b:Human error by drivers.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes happen because a driver did not see another vehicle or did something unexpected; human error is the primary cause.

question: When is it permitted to cross a dashed (broken) white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time.
note: Broken white lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only on hills.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a marked crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.,b:Only in a parking lot.,c:On a long driveway on private property.
note: It is unlawful to park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes; follow local parking rules and stay within 12 inches of the curb when parking on the street.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Driving aggressively to pass other drivers.,c:Following closely to control traffic flow.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid conflicts and collisions.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition carefully, apply brakes, and steer off the road to a safe area.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately.,c:Sound your horn continuously until help arrives.
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition (without locking the steering), apply the brakes, and move off the road safely.

question: If a driver's left arm is extended upward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn left.
note: A left arm extended upward by a driver is the hand signal for a right turn. Watch for that movement and adjust your driving accordingly.

question: How should drivers react to a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing yellow light is a warning; reduce speed and proceed through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous, and speeding is dangerous too.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are skilled.,c:Speed has no effect on crash seriousness.
note: Both driving too slowly and speeding can be hazardous; higher speeds increase the risk and severity of crashes.

question: How must you treat traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are mere suggestions.,c:Follow them only when other traffic is present.
note: Pavement markings, islands, signals, and signs control traffic and must be obeyed.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks with no signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Make sure there is room ahead so your vehicle can completely clear the tracks before you cross.,b:Assume you have right-of-way and proceed immediately.,c:Pass the vehicles ahead while crossing to get across faster.
note: Ensure there is enough space for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks; never stop on the tracks or pass while crossing.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn the wheels slightly to the right.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic.

question: Crosswalks are:
options: a:Always marked with vertical signs only.,b:Always marked on the pavement.,c:Either marked or unmarked; pedestrians still have crossing rights.
note: Crosswalks may be marked or unmarked; drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and stop behind the line as required.

question: About how many standard alcoholic drinks does the average body eliminate per hour?
options: a:About one standard drink per hour.,b:About three standard drinks per hour.,c:About two standard drinks per hour.
note: On average, a person’s body processes about one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck (no gates or flashing lights)?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio down to try to hear a train.,c:Proceed only when a flagger signals you to go.
note: Approach all railroad crossings with caution, look and listen for trains in both directions, and cross only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When in heavy construction-zone traffic only.
note: Driving significantly slower than the normal flow of traffic can be hazardous and may be illegal if it impedes other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At intersections of two similar roads without traffic control devices, you must yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

question: If the crossing signals at a railroad crossing are flashing, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and look for a train until the signals stop.,b:Slow down and proceed if you don't see a train.,c:Speed up to beat the train.
note: When railroad crossing signals are active, stop at a safe distance and wait until all warnings have ceased and it is clear to proceed.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:10 feet,b:15 feet,c:30 feet
note: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant so emergency crews can access it.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what should motorists do?
options: a:Communicate and signal clearly so motorcycles are not forced to change lanes or leave the roadway.,b:Assert right-of-way over motorcycles.,c:Ignore motorcycle presence if you are driving a larger vehicle.
note: Vehicle drivers should properly signal and communicate movements to motorcycle operators to avoid forcing them off the road.

question: How should you handle turns on slick or icy roads?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,c:Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum.
note: Approach curves and turns more slowly under slippery conditions to maintain control.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Both yellow and white.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: What happens if you refuse to take a chemical alcohol test when suspected of impaired driving?
options: a:Your license will be suspended.,b:You will be given a warning only.,c:You will get community service.
note: Operating a vehicle in North Carolina implies consent to a chemical test; refusal results in immediate license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,b:When you must drive off the pavement to complete the pass.,c:On a narrow bridge.,
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a lane to pass legally; you may not pass by driving off the pavement or on a narrow bridge.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Expose you to poisonous fumes and cause drowsiness while driving.,b:Increase oil consumption.,c:Reduce the need for routine maintenance.
note: A leaky exhaust can allow toxic gases into the vehicle cabin, causing drowsiness or death and making driving unsafe.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, gradually slow down, and pull off the road when safe.,b:Slam on your brakes immediately to stop as quickly as possible.,c:Keep speeding to reach the nearest service station quickly.
note: Do not abruptly apply the brakes. Grip the wheel firmly, reduce speed gradually, and pull off the road to a safe area.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a child who is about to run into the street.,b:When passing a bicyclist.,c:When traveling through an intersection.
note: Use the horn as a warning when someone may not see your vehicle, for example if a child runs into the street.

question: For a second conviction within one year of driving 55 mph when more than 15 mph over the limit, how long is the minimum license suspension?
options: a:60 days.,b:30 days.,c:10 days.
note: A second conviction for driving 55 mph or faster and exceeding the limit by 15 mph or more within one year results in at least a 60-day license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:All of the above.
note: When passing, signal well in advance (commonly at least 100 feet), check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot; return when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:It wakes you up and sharpens reflexes.,c:It only affects sleepiness, not reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reactions, impairing driving skills and judgment.

question: If you are involved in an accident and someone is injured, you should:
options: a:Not move the injured unless absolutely necessary; keep them warm and give first aid if trained.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene in all cases.,c:Always leave the injured where they are without offering any aid.
note: Do not move injured persons unnecessarily; untrained handling can worsen injuries. Keep them warm and provide first aid for severe bleeding until help arrives.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is headed into your lane, what initial actions should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake as needed.,b:Blow your horn, steer left into the oncoming lane, and accelerate.,c:Ignore it and maintain speed.
note: Honk to attract attention, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly; do not swerve into opposing traffic if possible.

question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or siren?
options: a:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if other vehicles yield first.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The largest vehicle regardless of arrival time.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive should proceed first. If two arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the right.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:Always stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if the way is clear, and you may turn unless a sign prohibits it.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign normally indicates:
options: a:A warning about a road hazard or special condition.,b:An interstate route marker.,c:A school crossing area.
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and indicate that you are approaching a hazardous location or an area where special rules apply.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on driving risk?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It lessens alcohol's effect on driving ability.
note: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can impair driving and combining them with alcohol increases crash risk.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That your emergency brake is applied.,c:That you are making a lane change.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping; they should always be in working order.

question: If you find yourself in another driver’s blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Stay at the same position and maintain speed.,c:Speed up and pass on the right.
note: Do not remain in someone else's blind spot; either move ahead or fall back to be visible in their mirrors.

question: How far ahead should good drivers try to see on the roadway?
options: a:Ten to fifteen seconds ahead.,b:Three seconds ahead.,c:Five seconds ahead.
note: Looking 10–15 seconds ahead helps you anticipate hazards and avoid last-minute maneuvers such as sudden stops or lane changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, what is essential to do?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn to warn oncoming traffic.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when making a left turn; proceed only when the way is clear.

question: How should you respond if another vehicle is tailgating you?
options: a:Move into the right lane if possible; if not, gradually reduce speed to encourage them to pass.,b:Brake sharply to warn the tailgater.,c:Maintain your speed and refuse to yield.
note: If being tailgated, move over to the right when safe. If you cannot, reduce speed slowly so the tailgater can pass; never brake abruptly.

question: To drive safely at night, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance, avoid driving if tired, and ensure headlights work properly.,b:Drive faster than daytime speeds because visibility is lower.,c:Rely solely on high beams at all times.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving when tired, and ensure headlights are in good condition.

question: What is the first adjustment you should make when getting into a car to drive?
options: a:Adjust your seat so you can reach controls and see clearly.,b:Adjust the rearview mirror first.,c:Fasten your seat belt last.
note: Set your seat position first so you can reach pedals and controls comfortably, then adjust mirrors and steering wheel.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow and a red light together means:
options: a:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow if the intersection is clear.,b:You may only go straight ahead.,c:You must wait for a steady green to move in any direction.
note: A green arrow allows movement only in the arrow's direction; the red light prohibits other movements while the arrow is displayed.

question: If you feel angry or upset when you get to your car, what is the safest course of action?
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,b:Drive fast to let off steam.,c:Play loud music to distract yourself.
note: Emotional upset can impair judgment; take time to calm down before driving to reduce crash risk.

question: Under the North Carolina point system, accumulating how many points within three years (after a prior suspension) will result in license suspension?
options: a:8 points if previously suspended; 12 points if not previously suspended.,b:10 points.,c:15 points.
note: If your license has been previously suspended, a subsequent accumulation of 8 points within three years will result in suspension; if never suspended previously, 12 points will lead to suspension.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Drive in the bike lane until you can pass.,b:Honk to instruct the bicyclist to move over.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible when passing.
note: Slow down and allow plenty of lateral space when passing a bicyclist; do not crowd or force them off the roadway.

question: When are roads most likely to become especially slippery?
options: a:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement becomes very slippery in the first 10–15 minutes of rainfall as water mixes with oils on the road surface, especially in hot conditions.

question: What is a likely result of combining alcohol with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing significant will happen.,c:The effects of both may be reduced.
note: Using alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp correctly?
options: a:Do not slow down until you have moved onto the exit ramp; then reduce speed.,b:Slow down on the main travel lane before entering the exit ramp.,c:Maintain the same freeway speed while on the exit ramp.
note: Do not slow down on the mainline; move into the exit lane and then decelerate on the ramp.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver who is tailgating you?
options: a:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to frighten them away.,c:Speed up to increase the gap to the vehicle ahead.
note: The safest response to a tailgater is to slow down gradually and let them pass when it is safe, or change lanes to get out of the way.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a:Steady red light.,b:Flashing yellow light.,c:Steady green light.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will soon change to a steady red light.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By reducing your ability to concentrate and increasing the chance of mistakes.,b:By lowering your chance of an accident.,c:By causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce concentration and impair driving ability; avoid driving if emotionally unstable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is true about driving well below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Driving significantly under the speed limit can be dangerous.,b:Driving below the limit is always the safest option.,c:Driving under the limit is the best way to avoid collisions.
note: Driving much slower than the posted speed can impede traffic flow and may force others to take risks while passing.

question: Alcohol consumption causes:
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.,b:Improved reaction times.,c:Increased alertness.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver attempts to pass your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Signal the passing driver when it is safe for them to pass.
note: When being passed, maintain a steady speed and, if needed, slightly reduce speed or move right when safe so the other vehicle can re-enter the lane.

question: What should you do immediately before changing lanes?
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Only check your side mirror once and move over.,c:Just look forward and turn your wheel.
note: Always check mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to ensure there are no vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:Unnecessary if you use mirrors.,b:A good driving habit and necessary to check areas mirrors don't show.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Mirrors do not show all areas; looking over your shoulder to check blind spots is an important safety practice.

question: May you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:No—you must stop and not go around or under the moving gate.,b:Yes, if you judge a train is not too close.,c:Yes, if your vehicle can pass without damaging the gate.
note: Lowered gates, flashing lights, or bells indicate a train is approaching—you must stop and may not go around or under a moving gate.

question: Which shape is exclusively used for stop signs?
options: a:An octagon (eight-sided) shape.,b:A square.,c:A circle.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) shape is used only for stop signs. Approach and come to a complete stop at these signs.

question: What is the recommended maximum speed when backing a vehicle?
options: a:10 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Back very slowly — generally not faster than 10 mph — because the vehicle is harder to control and stop while backing.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down but continue driving in the lane.,c:Drive with your hazard lights on until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren or lights, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential safe speeds depending on conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed that may be driven under ideal conditions.,c:The speed to use during heavy traffic only.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers must slow when conditions warrant.

question: How do eating and drinking while driving affect performance?
options: a:They distract the driver and increase the likelihood of leaving their lane or losing control.,b:They prevent drivers from making errors.,c:They make drivers better because they are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts your eyes and hands from driving, reducing control and increasing crash risk.

question: What is the purpose of highway markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:Provide information and guidance to drivers.,c:They are only used in construction zones.
note: Pavement markings inform drivers about lane positions, passing zones, and upcoming conditions to help maintain safe and orderly traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Required by law and a good driving habit.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Required only during the maneuver itself.
note: Signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires that you signal ahead of the maneuver (about 100 feet in urban areas).

question: When driving near heavy trucks, you should allow for:
options: a:The increased stopping distance and larger blind spots of large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,c:Reduced noise from larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require more stopping distance and have large blind spots. Stay where the truck driver can see you and avoid lingering in blind spots.

question: When is it permissible to consume alcoholic beverages on a public highway or sidewalk?
options: a:Only when the vehicle is parked off the roadway.,b:Never; it is illegal to consume alcoholic beverages on a public road or sidewalk.,c:Only if you are riding in the back seat.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage while on a public road or sidewalk; open containers are prohibited in areas occupied by driver or passengers.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and may be in blind spots.,b:They rarely use headlights.,c:Motorcyclists are generally less skilled drivers.
note: Motorcycles are smaller, can be hidden in blind spots, and it's often harder to judge their speed and distance; exercise extra caution.

question: Which statement about drowsy driving is correct?
options: a:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,b:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep you alert.,c:Drinking coffee always makes a drowsy driver safe to drive.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving performance similar to intoxication; simple measures like coffee or an open window are not reliable fixes.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning inside the vehicle.,b:It reduces the vehicle's top speed.,c:It causes a loss of hearing.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, which is odorless and can be deadly.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, it:
options: a:Slows your reactions and may make you feel overconfident.,b:Causes you to feel less confident.,c:Increases your metabolism of alcohol.
note: As alcohol builds up it slows reaction time and can create false confidence while impairing judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:Whoever moves first.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane, are you permitted to stop to drop off passengers or back up if you missed an entrance ramp?
options: a:No, you should not stop in a travel lane for such reasons.,b:You may stop briefly to drop off a passenger.,c:You may back up in the lane if you missed your turn.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. If you miss a turn or exit, proceed to the next safe location to turn around.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Keep the front wheels straight and rely only on the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area, what must you do to assist it?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Speed up to get out of the way at the last moment.,c:Stop immediately in the travel lane.
note: If safe, pull to the side to provide a clear path; do not block or stop in travel lanes unnecessarily.

question: How should you behave when approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop and yield.,b:Take the right-of-way immediately.,c:Proceed normally without slowing.
note: Yield to blind pedestrians and be prepared to stop so as not to endanger them; they have the right-of-way.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance in situations where visibility is reduced, in bad weather, when behind large vehicles that block your view, or when someone is tailgating you.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction?
options: a:Slow down, wait until traffic is clear, then pass leaving sufficient space (at least 3 feet).,b:Continue straight; the bicyclist must get out of your way.,c:Only pass at a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but allow extra lateral space (at least 3 feet) and only pass when safe.

question: Which conviction listed carries the highest number of points on your driving record?
options: a:Passing a stopped school bus (5 points),b:Driving recklessly (4 points),c:Driving on the wrong side of the road (4 points).
note: Passing a stopped school bus carries five points; reckless driving and driving on the wrong side carry fewer points.

question: What are you allowed to do when driving on a roadway marked by two solid yellow lines in the center?
options: a:Cross them only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross them to pass slower vehicles when the way looks clear.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Drive through until you feel the water deepen.,c:Proceed because standing water rarely gets deep.
note: Never attempt to drive through flooded roadways; the depth and current can be deceptive and can sweep a vehicle away.

question: When is it permissible to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:After the train has passed and it is safe to proceed.
note: Do not drive around lowered gates; wait until signals deactivate, gates are fully raised, and it is safe to cross.

question: What can speed up elimination of alcohol from a person's system?
options: a:Nothing — only time will allow alcohol to leave the body.,b:Cold showers.,c:Eating a large meal.
note: Alcohol is eliminated at a roughly constant rate by the body; nothing speeds the process appreciably — only time reduces BAC.

question: Which of the following is true under the point system for driver's records?
options: a:If you accumulate 12 points within three years, your license may be suspended.,b:A warning letter is always sent when you receive four points within three years.,c:You lose your license immediately upon getting 4 points.
note: Accumulating 12 points within a three-year period may result in license suspension. Other point thresholds trigger warnings or improvement classes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you merge into crowded freeway traffic?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to freeway traffic.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for space.,c:Enter at any speed and rely on others to make room.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to existing traffic.

question: Which statement best describes alcohol's effect on driving skills?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit affects driving.,c:Alcohol does not limit concentration or memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair driving skills and judgment; no amount of alcohol is safe for driving.

question: What are the colors of signs that indicate destination or highway exit information?
options: a:Green background with white letters.,b:Yellow background with black letters.,c:Red background with white letters.
note: Guide signs that provide directional and distance information are green with white letters or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which users?
options: a:Vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in the roundabout.,b:Only motor vehicles in the roundabout.,c:Only bicyclists in the roundabout.
note: Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians who are already in the roundabout before you enter.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and gradually slow before braking and pulling off the road.,b:Brake hard immediately to stop as quickly as possible.,c:Maintain speed and steer straight until reaching a repair shop.
note: If a tire blows out, keep control by steering straight, slowly reduce speed by easing off the accelerator, then brake gently and pull to a safe location.

question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow traffic light?
