options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination; it reduces a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:The lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.,b:The lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:A bicycle lane boundary.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; a solid white line indicates lane changing is discouraged or prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Enter the oncoming traffic lane when it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Never cross the centerline.,c:Use the shoulder to pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road typically requires moving briefly into the lane for oncoming traffic; only pass when it is legal and safe.

question: When approaching the scene of an accident, when should you stop?
options: a:Only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Keep your attention on your driving and keep going.,c:Always stop to look.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency assistance has not arrived; otherwise continue driving while watching for people or hazards.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns indicate?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You must stop before turning left.,c:You have the right-of-way to turn left without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: Which actions are important when you need to change lanes?
options: a:Signal ahead of the lane change, check your blind spot, and make sure the lane is clear before moving over.,b:Signal only after you begin the lane change.,c:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors.
note: Signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before changing positions to avoid collisions.

question: What lighting should you use if you must drive in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Hazard lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Turn on low beams when visibility is reduced; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign warn you about?
options: a:Existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:A nearby school zone.,c:Public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign that lacks a stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and ensuring it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing and verifying there is no cross traffic.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and only proceed when it is safe to do so.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane and give it full lane width.,b:Share the lane and drive partially beside the motorcycle.,c:Force the motorcycle to the right side of the lane.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane; give motorcyclists adequate space and do not crowd them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must drivers yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Only drivers who are already in the intersection.,c:Only pedestrians on the same side of the road as the turning vehicle.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Look in your rearview mirror only, then change lanes.,c:Turn on your signal after you begin to move.
note: Before changing lanes to the left, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your left shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a merging traffic sign on a multi-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over when safe.,b:Always maintain your current speed.,c:Honk at merging drivers to alert them.
note: When on a roadway with two or more lanes, make room for entering vehicles. Move over one lane if possible.

question: Which describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who stares off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:A person who maintains eye contact with a passenger while driving.,c:A driver who only watches the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Avoid distractions like daydreaming, looking at reading material, or sightseeing. Continually scan the road and mirrors.

question: Which method helps you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turning your head to look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change.,b:Using the inside rearview mirror alone.,c:Using the outside rearview mirror alone.
note: Mirrors do not show everything. You should turn your head to check blind spots before every lane change.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:You must always stop before crossing it.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and permits passing from either side when it is safe to do so.

question: What should you do to prepare for hazards ahead on the roadway?
options: a:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides for potential problems.,b:Stare straight ahead at the center of the road at all times.,c:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake when driving.
note: Search and identify potential problems early by scanning the road and roadside continuously.

question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass when safe.,b:Maintain your slow speed to be cautious.,c:Try to speed up to the posted limit immediately.
note: If you are impeding the normal flow of traffic on a two-lane, two-way road, pull off when safe to let vehicles pass to prevent hazards.

question: Which of these pavement devices is often used to direct drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Pavement arrows or lane-direction markings.,b:Flashing red lights over every lane.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement indicate which lanes are for turns or through movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and re-route from there.,b:Make a U-turn across the median to return to the exit.,c:Back up on the shoulder to return to the missed exit.
note: If you miss an exit, go to the next one. Do not stop, reverse, or cross a median on the freeway—it is illegal and dangerous.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: Always glance over the shoulder in the direction of the lane change to clear your blind spot; mirrors alone may not show everything.

question: If another car looks like it may hit you, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers only.
note: Use your horn as a warning if you believe another driver or pedestrian may not see you and a collision is imminent.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Stop your vehicle.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Determine whether anyone is injured.
note: If you are in a crash you must stop; then render aid, call emergency services if anyone is injured, and provide the required information to authorities.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and the time between drinks.,b:Only the amount of alcohol consumed.,c:Only the speed at which you drink.
note: Blood alcohol content depends on factors such as how much you drink, how fast you drink, your weight, and whether you've eaten; these affect absorption and impairment.

question: Which statement about sharing the road with motorcycles is correct?
options: a:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is acceptable for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,c:A two-person motorcycle is always more stable than a single-rider motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width. Be sure your vehicle is entirely in the adjacent lane before passing a motorcycle on the left.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect driving?
options: a:It is distracting and can reduce driving performance.,b:It helps you stay alert.,c:It has no effect on driving abilities.
note: Smoking requires hand and visual attention and can distract you from driving, increasing the likelihood of an error or crash.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn into a driveway or entrance.,b:To pass a slow-moving vehicle.,c:To pass another car in traffic.
note: You may cross double solid lines only to turn into or out of a driveway or entrance, or to make a permitted left turn or U-turn.

question: How should you check blind spots before turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.,b:Adjust the rearview mirror every few minutes.,c:Honk just before changing lanes.
note: Glancing over your shoulder in the direction of travel clears blind spots that mirrors may not show.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Make a sudden lane change to reach the exit.
note: Do not back up or make illegal turns on a freeway; use the next exit to reach your destination safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:As close as possible to the right side of the road.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: When preparing to make a right turn, move as far to the right as is practical and do not cut across lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the proper lane to make the desired turn, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
note: Do not make last-minute turns; continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these takes precedence over traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:Directions from a police officer or other authorized traffic control person.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.
note: Traffic officers (police, fire police, school crossing persons, work area flaggers) direct traffic and their directions override signs and signals.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Green.
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams, you should glance toward which part of the road?
options: a:The center.,b:The right side.,c:EITHER side,
note: When faced with glaring high beams, glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid temporary blindness.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They are likely blind and may require you to slow and yield.,b:They are always crossing illegally.,c:They are law enforcement officers.
note: Slow down and yield to pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog because they are likely blind and need extra protection.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals for rest and stretching.,b:Turn up the radio volume continuously.,c:Reduce your speed and drive more slowly without breaks.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch to avoid drowsiness on long trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may:
options: a:Still make the turn indicated by the arrow but must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:No longer turn and must proceed straight, even if turning is safe.,c:Continue turning without yielding because you had the arrow earlier.
note: A green arrow gives protected turn movement; when it becomes a steady green you may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while driving uphill, what should you keep in mind?
options: a:The truck may be traveling below the posted speed limit and you may not be able to safely pass.,b:You can always pass if you have enough speed.,c:It is always legal to pass on a hill.
note: Large vehicles often slow on inclines and visibility on hills is limited; you may not be able to pass safely or legally on a hill with limited sight distance.

question: What factors affect the space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.,b:The presence of a stop sign alone.,c:Whether you signaled earlier.
note: Space required depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see and may behave unpredictably.,b:They always obey different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are often harder to see and can be less protected; be alert and give them space.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The medicine cancels out the alcohol.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work faster.
note: Combining alcohol with medicines can increase impairment and multiply harmful effects, making driving dangerous.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do to make your vehicle visible?
options: a:Turn on your hazard (emergency) flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve the battery.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: When stopped at night, use emergency flashers and leave your low-beam headlights on so other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you enter?
options: a:The right lane of the one-way street.,b:The center of the street.,c:The left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane that is legally available.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may not pass or change lanes.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may cross the line to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. A single dashed white line means drivers may cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, the safest practice is to:
options: a:Drive at the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than other vehicles to avoid congestion.,c:Drive significantly slower than other traffic to remain cautious.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers travel much faster or slower than the flow of traffic. Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limit.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming high beams at night, you should focus your vision:
options: a:On the center of the road directly ahead.,b:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,c:Over your shoulder at oncoming headlights.
note: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, look toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded.

question: If you begin to drive in sleet or snow, what should you do?
options: a:Allow additional following distance and keep windshield and mirrors clear.,b:Increase your speed so you reach your destination faster.,c:Drive as you normally would in dry conditions.
note: Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance because slippery surfaces increase stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a transit bus is signaling to re-enter the roadway after stopping to load passengers, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the left lane if it is clear.,b:Yield to the bus by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping.,c:Honk to alert the driver of your presence.
note: Yield to any transit vehicle signaling to re-enter the main roadway after a stop; change lanes, slow, or stop to allow safe re-entry.

question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:
options: a:You cannot see without turning your head.,b:You see only in the rearview mirror.,c:Directly behind your vehicle.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with mirrors alone; you must move your head to check them before changing lanes.

question: What is a “No zone”?
options: a:The large blind spot around a truck or other large vehicle.,b:A designated no-passing zone.,c:A one-way traffic area.
note: 'No zones' are large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver's view; avoid lingering there.

question: If another driver aggressively cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Stay calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: Avoid escalation: remain calm, slow down or change lanes to let the aggressive driver pass, and avoid confrontations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Turn on your hazard flashers and continue driving.
note: On a one-way street you must drive toward the nearest roadside and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, signal, find a gap, and merge safely into traffic.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a specific instruction are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs convey laws and rules that drivers must obey; failure to comply may result in a penalty.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection and proceed when clear.,b:Stop if a nearby police officer signals you to do so.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and stop before proceeding.
note: When approaching a steady green light you may continue through the intersection but must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles already in the intersection. Approach at a speed that allows you to stop if the light changes.

question: Which driving habit will help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from a stop.,b:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.,c:Idling in the driveway with the engine running.
note: Smooth driving—anticipating traffic, avoiding rapid acceleration and unnecessary braking—improves fuel economy.

question: When backing up, you should:
options: a:Turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window rather than relying only on mirrors.,b:Rely only on mirrors and sensors.,c:Always depend solely on a backup camera.
note: Turn your head and look back when backing; do not rely exclusively on mirrors or cameras.

question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow for turning?
options: a:Slow and stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is coming.,b:Merge into the lane in the arrow's direction.,c:Proceed to turn after yielding to pedestrians only.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is coming; stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive simultaneously and the other vehicle is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the other vehicle through the intersection.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right and allow it to proceed.,c:Enter the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and pull off to a safe area to stop.,b:Turn off your hazard lights and immediately stop in the travel lane.,c:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
note: Loss of power steering increases steering effort required; slow down, steer carefully to a safe area, and stop.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Firmly apply the brakes.,c:Apply the parking brake.
note: First reduce speed by taking your foot off the accelerator; if more slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines can all impair driving.
note: Many kinds of drugs—including illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and some over-the-counter remedies—can affect your ability to drive safely.

question: What should drivers do in bad weather regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Increase their speed to reach their destination faster.,c:Decrease their following distance.
note: In poor weather, increase the following distance to give yourself more time to react and stop safely.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside such vehicles and do not tailgate.,b:Flash your headlights at them to get their attention.,c:Never pass them under any circumstances.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots at their sides and rear; avoid these areas and give them extra room when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to steady yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if not, proceed with caution.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and always continue through.,c:Stop immediately no matter how close you are to the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon be red; stop if it is safe to do so, otherwise clear the intersection carefully.

question: A key trait of a good defensive driver is:
options: a:Watching and anticipating the actions of other drivers.,b:Always driving slowly regardless of conditions.,c:Maintaining a constant speed at all times.
note: A defensive driver expects other drivers' actions and anticipates problems to reduce crash risk.

question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic so you can blend in safely.,b:Proceed slowly and wait indefinitely for an opening.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until you are fully merged.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speed and merge smoothly, yielding to traffic already on the freeway.

question: If you become stranded during a snowstorm, what is the safest action?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk along the road to find help.,c:Lie down inside the vehicle and go to sleep.
note: If stranded in severe winter weather, remain in your vehicle, conserve heat, and wait for help—the vehicle is easier for rescuers to spot than a person on foot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At speeds of 45 mph or higher, how far in advance should you signal before turning?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet
note: When driving faster (about 45 mph or more), signal at least 200 feet before you make the turn or change lanes.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:
options: a:Get out of the aggressive driver’s way and avoid eye contact or confrontation.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass to show disapproval.,c:Speed up to try to escape their aggression.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, make every effort to get out of their way; do not engage or escalate the situation.

question: Before starting down a steep hill, what gear selection is advisable if possible?
options: a:Shift into a lower gear to help control speed.,b:Shift into a higher gear to save fuel.,c:Come to a complete stop at the top.
note: Shifting to a lower gear helps avoid excessive brake use and provides better speed control downhill.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers checking mirrors frequently.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way properly.
note: Driving too fast for current road, weather, or traffic conditions is a frequent factor in crashes.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You become less alert.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance improves.,c:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
note: Alcohol reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and distorts judgment of speed and distance.

question: If your right wheels run off the pavement, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, then ease back onto the pavement.,b:Stop immediately and get out of the vehicle.,c:Accelerate and quickly steer back onto the road.
note: Do not panic. Remove your foot from the accelerator, steer parallel to the roadway, slow, and when it is safe, ease back onto the pavement.

question: How does increasing your speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you have less time to perceive and react to hazards.

question: Approaching an unmarked railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop even if no train is visible.,c:Assume all crossings have signals so you can proceed normally.
note: At unmarked crossings slow and be ready to stop; ensure no train is approaching before proceeding.

question: An advisory speed sign attached to a curve indicates:
options: a:A recommended speed that should be reduced further in rain, snow, or ice.,b:A speed you can ignore in severe weather.,c:That the posted speed limit does not apply in curves.
note: Advisory speeds suggest a safe speed for curves; drivers should reduce speed even more in poor weather conditions.

question: A pedestrian walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be what?
options: a:Blind or visually impaired.,b:Deaf.,c:Part of a traffic study.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog and exercise extra caution.

question: What does a double solid yellow center line mean?
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: Yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic. Solid lines indicate passing is prohibited.

question: During normal driving conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.
note: Keep a minimum two-second following distance in normal weather and traffic; increase it in poor conditions.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before applying the brakes.,b:Stop suddenly to alert drivers behind you.,c:Quickly change lanes before stopping.
note: Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas so the vehicle slows before you apply steady brake pressure to stop smoothly.

question: If your license has not previously been suspended, it will be suspended for accumulating how many points within three years?
options: a:12 points.,b:10 points.,c:15 points.
note: If you accumulate 12 points within a three-year period and your license has not previously been suspended, your license may be suspended.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what helps ensure a safe ride home?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving while impaired; coffee or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

question: What is the primary purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.,b:They are placed only where there is an immediate danger.,c:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what actions are required or prohibited (e.g., speed limits, no-turn signs). They are often rectangular and use black on white or red markings.

question: A driver taking an over-the-counter medicine should:
options: a:Read the drug label and check for warnings about driving impairment.,b:Drink alcohol to counteract drowsiness.,c:Assume all OTC drugs are safe for driving.
note: Many OTC medicines can affect driving ability. Read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist about driving while using them.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning, which actions are recommended?
options: a:Maintain good tire tread and proper inflation, and reduce speed in the rain.,b:Always use cruise control in wet conditions.,c:Drive faster through puddles to avoid hydroplaning.
note: Good tire tread and correct inflation plus reduced speed in wet conditions help prevent hydroplaning.

question: When must drivers use headlights?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less.,b:Only when it is raining.,c:Only during heavy traffic.
note: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is 400 feet or less; use low beams in rain.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what is one of the first things you should do?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene and, if possible, move it out of traffic.,b:Stand in traffic lanes to direct other vehicles.,c:Leave the scene if the damage is minor.
note: Stop at or near the crash scene, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can, turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles, and avoid standing in traffic lanes.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a three-lane roadway, you must:
options: a:Stop until the bus's stop arm is retracted and lights stop flashing.,b:Proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Honking before passing to alert children.
note: Drivers must stop for a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended; wait until the arm is retracted and the lights stop before proceeding.

question: When meeting a car with blinding headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,c:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
note: If another driver has their high beams on, avoid direct stare at the lights and glance toward the right edge of the road until they pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic light tells drivers to:
options: a:Stop and yield.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Yield to pedestrians only.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal changes to green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly to allow others to go first.
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to vehicles and pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On dry paved highways under ideal conditions.,c:When driving in daylight only.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose surfaces; increase following distance accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What speed must you not exceed while driving?
options: a:A speed that is greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.,b:The posted maximum speed only.,c:Any speed as long as it feels safe to you.
note: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions: adjust speed for traffic, weather, and visibility even if below the posted limit.

question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop when:
options: a:Flashing red lights are activated, a crossing gate is lowered, or a stop sign is posted.,b:Only if the crossing lights are flashing.,c:Only if a crossing gate is lowered.
note: You must stop for flashing red lights, lowered gates, posted stop signs, flaggers, or when a train is visible or close enough to be hazardous.

question: Which is a risk of driving with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Tires can increase your stopping distance.,b:Tires make turning easier.,c:Tires eliminate hydroplaning risk.
note: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning more difficult, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What action should you take when you encounter a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are also approaching.,c:Stop only if cars are already in the intersection.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can fully pass through it.,b:Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.,c:Enter the intersection slowly and wait.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking the intersection is illegal and creates hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and the way ahead is clear after the vehicles in front have moved, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping again.,b:Come to a complete stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or line before proceeding, even if traffic ahead has already moved.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop, then proceed only when it is safe.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop; proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see their turn signals.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time and increases the risk of a rear-end collision if the lead vehicle brakes suddenly.

question: What does a pavement arrow painted in a lane require drivers in that lane to do?
options: a:Drivers in that lane are required to follow the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers in that lane may choose a different movement if traffic is light.,c:Drivers must stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
note: A pavement arrow shows the traffic movement required from that lane; follow any traffic signs or signals before making the indicated movement.

question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do if it is safe to do so?
options: a:Move over to another lane and slow down to give extra space; if you cannot change lanes, slow down.,b:Drive to the right and stop directly next to the vehicle.,c:Remain in your lane and continue at the same speed.
note: When approaching stopped emergency, roadside assistance, or tow vehicles with flashing lights, change lanes away if possible and slow down if not.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the pavement?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:In curves and on hills.
note: Stop lines mark the place where drivers must stop at intersections or before crosswalks and are painted as solid white lines across the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Only a suggested speed.,c:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket.
note: A speed limit indicates the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you should drive slower when conditions are hazardous.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light will soon be red.,b:You have the right-of-way to speed through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop immediately no matter where you are.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red; slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides.,c:On all sides of the vehicle when possible.
note: Maintain a cushion of space around your vehicle—front, rear, and both sides—to allow time to react to traffic situations.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Whenever you are changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward/away from a curb.,b:Only when pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Only when pulling out of a parking space.
note: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder every time you change the vehicle's position (lane changes, turns, curb maneuvers).

question: What is a good practice to relieve fatigue on long trips?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Do arm exercises while driving every hour.,c:Drive with one eye closed occasionally to stay alert.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop every two hours for a short break. If drowsy, pull off and rest or find a safe place to stay overnight.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Night driving.,c:Slow speeds.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the severity of collisions; always drive at speeds appropriate to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Only when visible traffic is present.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Always signal to communicate your intended movements to others, even if you think no one else is present.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive the posted speed limit and be cautious.,c:Increase your speed to maintain control.
note: Reduce your speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet. Driving more slowly than the posted speed may be necessary for safety.

question: A sign reading Reduced speed 35 mph means what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the sign.,b:The reduced speed zone begins at the next sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
note: Reduced speed signs indicate that the new speed limit begins at the sign unless another sign specifies otherwise.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: Large tractor-trailers require significantly longer stopping distances than cars; at 55 mph a fully loaded truck can require nearly 400 feet to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal light means you must:
options: a:Stop at the marked stop line, before entering the crosswalk, or before the intersection.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A red signal requires stopping at the stop line, before entering any crosswalk, or before the intersection if no stop line or crosswalk is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver’s left arm is extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:The driver plans to stop.,b:The driver plans to turn left.,c:The driver plans to turn right.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver intends to stop; adjust your driving accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a legal and safe circumstance to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only when the dividing line is broken and it is safe to do so.,b:By driving onto the shoulder of the road.,c:On a hill or in a curve because you assume no oncoming traffic.,d:When your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane looks clear.
note: You may pass another vehicle only where it is legal and safe, such as where the centerline is broken; never pass on a shoulder, hill, or curve where you cannot see oncoming traffic or over a solid line.

question: How should you respond if you see other drivers acting angrily or aggressively?
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation — do not engage or make eye contact.,b:Return aggressive gestures to assert yourself.,c:Drive closer to intimidate them.
note: Avoid eye contact or gestures, and put distance between you and an aggressive driver by slowing, changing lanes, or pulling over when safe.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition key?
options: a:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,b:Turn off the engine only.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: Whenever you leave a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before beginning to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:Early enough so other drivers understand your intentions (e.g., at least 100 feet in many conditions).,c:After you start the lane change.
note: Signal early to let other drivers know your intentions in advance; in many situations you should signal at least 100 feet before the maneuver.

question: What color are signs that indicate public recreation or cultural interest areas?
options: a:Brown.,b:Orange.,c:Green.
note: Brown signs designate areas of cultural, historical, or recreational interest and help guide travelers.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in the street?
options: a:Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they appear to be crossing against a light or acting carelessly.

question: Signs that warn of potentially hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions so they can take appropriate action.

question: What is the “No zone” around large trucks or buses?
options: a:The blind spots around the truck or bus where other vehicles disappear from the driver's view.,b:A special reduced speed zone.,c:An area where loud music is prohibited.
note: Large trucks and buses have significant blind spots on several sides; these areas are called 'No zones.' Avoid lingering there.

question: What do pennant-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are used to warn drivers of upcoming no-passing zones.

question: Which of these is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes and making jerking motions.,b:Constantly checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Consistently yielding the right-of-way.
note: Typical signs of impairment include weaving, sudden speed changes, swerving, and erratic braking.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require less stopping distance than cars.,b:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,c:Have a smaller turning radius than cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more distance to slow and stop; allow extra space when driving near them.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,b:Try to pass any stopped train quickly.,c:Drive faster to cross before the train arrives.
note: Railroad warning signs mean be alert and be prepared to stop for approaching trains or for active crossing signals.

question: In which situation must a person have a driver license?
options: a:To steer a vehicle that is being towed or pushed.,b:To unlock a passenger door.,c:To buckle a child into a restraint system.
note: It is unlawful to sit in the front seat and steer a vehicle being towed or pushed without a valid driver license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Excessive speed for the driving conditions.,b:Always driving at the posted speed.,c:Using turn signals when required.
note: Driving too fast for road or weather conditions is a major cause of crashes; inattention and tailgating also contribute.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color?
options: a:White.,b:Blue.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs that control traffic movement are typically white with black markings and must be obeyed.

question: What helps you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk to alert other drivers of your presence.,c:Drive in the right lane only.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead lets you react smoothly and reduces the need for sudden emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the roadway and proceed only when no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching.,b:Honk to warn approaching traffic and then enter.,c:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles to move out of the way.
note: Always stop before crossing the sidewalk and yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians before entering the roadway.

question: If the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger, you should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space.,b:Avoid following their example.,c:Assume they present no additional risk.
note: Distracted drivers reduce their safety margin. Allow extra space between your vehicle and a distracted driver to reduce collision risk.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to do what?
options: a:Stop, then proceed when safe (same as a stop sign).,b:Yield only to oncoming traffic.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: come to a full stop, then proceed when the way is clear.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down and turn on headlights; stop on the shoulder if visibility becomes unsafe.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to reduce exposure time.
note: Reduce speed when rain reduces visibility, use headlights, and if visibility becomes too poor, pull safely off the road and wait.

question: If your vehicle hits an unattended parked vehicle and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written note with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.,b:Drive away and report it later if you remember.,c:Call a tow truck and leave the scene.
note: If you cannot locate the owner, leave a written note giving your name, address, and details of the incident, and report the accident as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A “No standing” sign means:
options: a:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers.,b:You may park there if you remain in the vehicle.,c:You may never stop there for any reason.
note: No standing means you may briefly stop to drop off or pick up passengers, but you may not park there.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive and lead to a DUII?
options: a:Alcoholic beverages only.,b:Prescription or illegal drugs only.,c:All types listed, including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications.
note: A wide range of substances—including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over-the-counter medications—can impair driving.

question: What is the proper order of traffic lights from top to bottom on a vertical signal?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, yellow, red.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: On vertical signals, red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced and you cannot see as well as in daylight.,b:Traffic volume is higher at night.,c:All vehicles travel faster at night.
note: Darkness reduces visibility; headlights are required from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise or when visibility is under 500 feet.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped on the opposite side of a center turning lane on a four-lane roadway, drivers may:
options: a:Continue driving but exercise extra caution.,b:Must stop until the bus moves.,c:Stop until the stop arm is lifted regardless of lane layout.
note: On a four-lane roadway with a center turn lane separating opposing traffic, drivers on the opposite side may proceed but should be cautious.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering a public road from a private driveway should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic if needed.
note: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already using the public roadway and merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has more than one lane in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:The middle lane always.,c:The lane marked with an arrow only.
note: When turning, enter the lane nearest to the one you were in and avoid changing lanes during the turn.

question: How would you classify distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Not a concern for safe drivers.
note: Distracted driving greatly increases crash risk because it reduces awareness and reaction ability.

question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed through the entire curve.,c:Speed up when entering and slow down when exiting.
note: Slow down before entering a curve and increase speed gradually as you exit to maintain traction and control.

question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop when displayed?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: Hydroplaning is most often caused by what?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet road conditions so tires cannot clear water.,b:Excessive stops on dry roads.,c:Sudden braking on dry pavement.
note: Tires can lose contact with the road when driving too quickly on a water-covered surface, causing hydroplaning.

question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:The driver and all passengers in vehicles equipped with seat belts.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only front seat passengers.
note: In North Carolina the driver and all passengers in a vehicle equipped with seat belts must have them properly fastened whenever the vehicle is in forward motion on a street or highway.

question: Vehicle stopping distances do NOT depend on which of the following?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle condition, road and weather conditions, and speed—not on the time of day itself.

question: Which sections of road tend to freeze first in cold or wet weather?
options: a:Road sections shaded by trees or buildings.,b:Roads in open sunlit areas.,c:Flat, unshaded stretches only.
note: Shaded areas receive less sunlight and often remain icy or wet longer, so they freeze sooner and dry more slowly than surrounding pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a roadway center has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Cross the lines to pass when traffic is clear.,b:Never pass under any circumstances.,c:Pass only in an emergency.
note: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,b:It helps driving skills while harming judgment.,c:It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.
note: Alcohol degrades many abilities needed for safe driving, including reaction time, perception, coordination, and judgment.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Assume it is safe to cross immediately.,b:Look and listen for another train on the other track before crossing.,c:Cross quickly while the first train is still clearing the area.
note: Where two or more tracks exist, always check for additional trains before proceeding; another train may be approaching on the adjacent track.

question: What is important to remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain; reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Wet roads never affect stopping distance.,c:You can use cruise control in heavy rain.
note: Roads are often most slippery just after rain begins; slow down and give yourself extra stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it necessary to signal?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into/out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Only during nighttime driving.
note: Use turn signals whenever you intend to change your vehicle's direction or position, so other road users know your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is present?
options: a:The funeral procession has the right-of-way.,b:Another driver has the right-of-way.,c:A pedestrian has the right-of-way.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists should yield to funeral processions; the procession may proceed through intersections together.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, the safest response is to:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely.,b:Pull next to them and yell.,c:Flash your high beams aggressively.
note: To avoid road rage and reduce crash risk, accept the mistake and continue driving safely without retaliation.

question: When approaching a curve in the roadway, drivers should slow down:
options: a:Before entering the curve.,b:After completing the curve.,c:Only if a warning sign is posted.
note: Adjust your speed before entering a curve; entering too quickly can cause loss of traction.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb (to the right).,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (to the left).
note: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll away from traffic.

question: About what portion of all traffic fatalities involve alcohol?
options: a:About 38 percent.,b:About 60 percent.,c:About 24 percent.
note: Drunk driving contributes to a large share of traffic fatalities—approximately 38 percent.

question: Which recommendation does not directly improve safe driving at night?
options: a:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle.,b:Keeping your windshield clean.,c:Being aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.
note: While a flashlight may be useful in an emergency, it is not a primary measure for improving driving visibility at night; keeping windows clean and recognizing limitations from tinting are more directly helpful.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:Only if you are driving behind it on a multi-lane highway.,b:When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.,c:Only when children are in sight on the road.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic from both directions must stop whenever a stopped school bus displays flashing red lights or extends its stop arm.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line only.
note: When a broken yellow line is beside a solid yellow line, traffic beside the broken line may pass when safe; traffic beside the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which condition must be met before you can safely pass on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:You can see the road ahead clearly and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are traveling faster than the speed limit.,c:You are near the top of a hill.
note: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road you must see far enough ahead, be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have adequate speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you check before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Mirrors and blind spots, and signal before you pass.,b:Sound your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, then pass only when it is safe and you can return to your lane without cutting off the other vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private drive or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.,b:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.,c:Sound your horn to warn other drivers.
note: You must yield to all pedestrians and roadway traffic when entering from a private road or driveway.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to locate and test the controls and check for defects.,b:Ignore any unfamiliar controls because all vehicles operate the same.,c:Hide from the owner that you do not know how to operate it.
note: When using an unfamiliar vehicle, familiarize yourself with turn signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, horn, and correct any defects before driving.

question: What colors are standard warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:White letters or symbols on a blue background.,b:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.,c:Black letters or symbols on a white background.
note: Most warning signs that signal potential hazards are yellow with black lettering or symbols; work zone warnings are typically orange with black symbols.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the directions of the flagger.,b:Copy the actions of the surrounding traffic instead of the flagger.,c:Assume the flagger is mistaken and ignore them.
note: Flaggers control traffic in work zones for safety; you must obey their directions and be prepared to reduce speed.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on your side mirrors.,c:Check the rearview mirror only.
note: In addition to mirror checks, glance over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot before moving laterally.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on snow or ice?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Add heavy weight to the vehicle's trunk.,c:Get off the highway as quickly as possible.
note: Slower speeds and much greater following distances are the most effective ways to reduce the risk of a crash on snow- or ice-covered roads.

question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is generally:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from lights, and increased likelihood of fatigued or impaired drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Vary your speed — generally reduce it so you can maintain control.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection faster.,c:Maintain the same speed as before the turn.
note: Reduce speed to a safe level that allows you to control the vehicle and react to unexpected events while turning.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Stop.,b:Speed limit.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An octagon sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop at it.

question: When children are playing near the street, you should expect that they may:
options: a:Always wait for traffic to clear before crossing.,b:Run into the street without looking.,c:Signal before crossing.
note: Children may not recognize traffic dangers and can run out into the street unexpectedly; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,b:School zone ahead.,c:Construction area ahead.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign; yield when required and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested speed only for bad weather.,c:A recommended speed for light traffic times.
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust speed lower for poor conditions.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:If you lose control of your vehicle and need to warn others.,b:When passing another car on the highway.,c:To signal dissatisfaction with another driver.
note: Use your horn to alert others to an immediate danger (for example, if you lose control), not to express frustration.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turning on your windshield wipers.,b:Reducing your speed.,c:Turning on interior lights.
note: Decrease your speed first to increase reaction time and allow for safer vehicle control when visibility drops.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Wait until police arrive before moving anything.,c:Leave the vehicle where it is under all circumstances.
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe to do so, but do not leave the scene without providing required information.

question: In what ways can alcoholic beverages affect you?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking, and can give false confidence.,b:They always improve coordination.,c:They make you more alert and cautious.
note: Alcohol dulls parts of the brain controlling judgment and self-control, slows reaction time, and impairs vision and distance judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at an intersection with a green light but oncoming traffic is heavy. You should:
options: a:Enter the intersection and wait in the center only if it is legal and safe to do so, then complete the turn when clear.,b:Use the next intersection to turn around instead of waiting.,c:Wait in the center of the intersection regardless of traffic rules.
note: You may move into the intersection to wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic if the light is green and it is legal to enter; otherwise wait behind the crosswalk.

question: If you are upset, worried, or distracted before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Start driving and hope you calm down.,b:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.,c:Drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Strong emotions can impair driving; take time to calm down and focus before you begin driving.

question: Any activity that causes you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,b:Only take your hands off the wheel.,c:Only take your eyes off the instrument panel.
note: Anything that takes your attention, eyes, or hands away from driving is a distraction and increases crash risk.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck that carries flammable liquids, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.,b:Pass them on the right when possible.,c:Decrease your following distance to see better.
note: School buses and tank vehicles carrying flammable liquids must stop at railroad crossings; be prepared to stop when following them.

question: What is the DMV consequence if you refuse a requested chemical test?
options: a:Immediate revocation of your license for at least 30 days plus an additional revocation of at least 12 months by the DMV.,b:Placement on probation.,c:Assignment to a driver improvement program only.
note: Refusing a chemical test leads to immediate license revocation (at least 30 days) and an additional administrative revocation (typically at least 12 months) by the DMV.

question: When starting a parallel park between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space, then begin the backing maneuver.,b:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels sharply to the right immediately.
note: Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the empty space, signal, then back in while turning the wheel as required to fit into the space.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles.,b:Entering a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Using crosswalks when vehicles are stopped.
note: Even though pedestrians have rights, do not step into crosswalks or roadways when vehicles are approaching and might not have time to stop.

question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Black.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a multilane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:The passing lane is clear before changing lanes.,b:You only pass on the right.,c:There is oncoming traffic in the other lane.
note: Before passing, confirm the passing lane is clear and signal to change lanes.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle.,b:Only the person driving.,c:Only passengers on long highway trips.
note: Every person in the vehicle should wear a seat belt; unbelted occupants become dangerous projectiles in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on interstate highways in North Carolina?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: Unless posted otherwise, the maximum speed limit on interstates is 70 mph; always obey posted speed limit signs.

question: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:No headlights — use parking lights.
note: Use low beams when another vehicle is approaching or when following within 500 feet to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: Approximately what percentage of traffic fatalities involve alcohol?
options: a:About 38 percent.,b:About 10 percent.,c:About 18 percent.
note: Alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely. About 38 percent of all traffic fatalities involve alcohol.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you drive?
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: Be alert for children near school crossings and be prepared to stop when they are present or about to cross.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing the bicyclist?
options: a:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.,b:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,c:Split the difference and squeeze through.
note: When faced with multiple hazards, deal with them one at a time: wait for the oncoming car to pass, then safely pass the bicyclist.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities - (Registration, insurance, equipment requirements, accident procedures)
question: When setting the inside rearview mirror, you should position it so you can clearly see:
options: a:Your own reflection.,b:The entire rear window.,c:Only the rear seat passengers.,d:Both side mirrors.
note: Adjust the inside rearview mirror so the full rear window is visible from the driver's seated position. You should be able to check it by moving only your eyes, not your head.

question: When riding in a vehicle, small children should:
options: a:Be properly restrained in child safety seats appropriate for their size and age.,b:Be held by a strong adult on the seat.,c:Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
note: Children should be secured in properly installed child seats; no adult can reliably hold a child in place during a crash or sudden stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely.,b:Honk to clear them out of the way.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if you have a green light; be especially cautious around pedestrians in all circumstances.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Only half the lane width.,c:Use of bicycle lanes as needed.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, same as other vehicles.

question: What does an End School Zone sign indicate?
options: a:The start of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The end of the reduced speed school zone.,c:A 20 mph speed limit begins.
note: The End School Zone sign indicates the end of the reduced speed area for the school zone.

question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,b:Increase your speed to merge, then turn.,c:Turn the steering wheel early and then signal.
note: Signal three to four seconds before your turn so other drivers know your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer stops your vehicle, how should you behave until the officer approaches?
options: a:Stay in the vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and open your door immediately.,c:Get out of the vehicle and walk to the officer.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible, have passengers keep hands in view, and wait until the officer requests documents or other actions.

question: When is it important to reduce your speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections or railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery.,b:Only when other drivers ask you to slow down.,c:Only on rural roads.
note: Slow down in narrow or winding areas, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills and sharp curves, and when conditions (wet or icy) make driving hazardous.

question: Which actions require a valid driver license? (I) Sitting in the driver's seat while the engine is running. (II) Steering a car being pushed or towed.
options: a:Both I & II,b:I only,c:II only
note: In North Carolina it is illegal to sit in the driver's seat with the engine running or to steer a vehicle being pushed or towed unless you have a valid driver's license.

question: Which of these is not a major factor in determining your vehicle's total stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.
note: Total stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor.

question: What effect can drinking alcohol while also taking drugs have?
options: a:It can increase the effects of both the alcohol and the drugs.,b:It will decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,c:It will help the medication work faster.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can multiply impairing effects and make driving much more dangerous.

question: Car drivers should be aware that large trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need extra room for maneuvers.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and need more space to stop and maneuver than passenger cars.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly and give it extra room.,b:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,c:Honk continuously to scare it away.
note: Be very cautious around animals on the road; pass slowly to avoid startling or frightening them.

question: Which statement about pedestrian fatalities is correct?
options: a:In cities, about two of every five people killed by motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians.,b:Most pedestrians killed in all traffic crashes are teenagers.,c:Pedestrians are rarely killed in urban crashes.
note: In urban areas, a substantially higher proportion of traffic fatalities are pedestrians compared to rural areas; the teenager statement is incorrect.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel into the direction of the skid.,b:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,c:Overcorrect the steering sharply.
note: If the vehicle begins to skid, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain traction.

question: May you park or stop along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,b:Yes, anytime if you turn on your hazard flashers.,c:Yes, if you are checking a map for directions.
note: Parking on the shoulder of a freeway is prohibited except in emergencies.

question: Which of the following is true regarding seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:You should always make sure all passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,b:You may place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat if the airbag is turned off.,c:Airbags are safe for rear-facing infant restraints in the front seat.
note: Ensure all passengers are properly restrained; children 12 and under should ride in the rear seat, and never place a rear-facing infant in front of an active airbag.

question: Which of the following is the most distracting and increases crash risk?
options: a:Using a cell phone while driving.,b:Changing the radio station.,c:Listening to the CD player only.
note: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) is a significant distraction and increases crash risk.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Single broken yellow.,c:Combination solid and broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing for traffic in both directions.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
