options: a:Drive more quickly to get through wet patches faster.,b:Drive more slowly and reduce your speed.,c:Drive through deeper water to maintain control.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds on wet pavement; reducing speed and avoiding standing water lowers the risk.

question: Which is true about a work zone?
options: a:It may be stationary or moving and requires extra caution.,b:It is always marked with black and white signs.,c:You do not need to slow down in work zones.
note: Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked by orange signs; slow down and pay extra attention.

question: About 38 percent of all traffic fatalities involve which of the following?
options: a:Alcohol only.,b:Multiple-vehicle crashes only.,c:Both alcohol and multiple-vehicle crashes.
note: Approximately 38 percent of traffic fatalities involve alcohol impairment.

question: What color are guide or destination signs that give directional and mileage information?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide signs that provide directional and mileage information are green with white letters and symbols.

question: Larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Larger blind spots than smaller vehicles.,b:Smaller blind spots than cars.,c:No blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Avoid lingering where truck drivers cannot see you.

question: Which medications might negatively affect your driving ability?
options: a:Any medication that may cause drowsiness or impair judgment.,b:Only headache medicine.,c:Only diet pills.
note: Many prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Always read labels and ask your doctor or pharmacist about driving while on medications.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to make a left turn?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady green left-turn arrow.,c:A solid green circular light.
note: A steady green arrow for left turns gives you the right-of-way to make that turn; oncoming traffic must yield.

question: If your wheels slip off the road edge while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gently while keeping wheels off the pavement, then steer back onto the road when safe.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle onto the pavement.,c:Slam on your brakes immediately.
note: Do not force the vehicle back onto the pavement. Reduce speed gently, then return to the pavement at a safe speed.

question: If you hear a siren while driving, you should:
options: a:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop immediately where you are without signaling.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, reduce speed and move to the curb or edge of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view, what is the proper action?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before starting the turn.,b:Accelerate rapidly once the first lane is clear.,c:Wave an oncoming driver to let you go first.
note: Never begin a left turn unless you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can complete the turn safely.

question: Which of the following can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,b:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,c:Changing a radio station or CD.
note: Many activities—such as eating, talking on a phone, or adjusting the radio—can divert your attention from driving and create dangerous distractions.

question: When is it acceptable to stop your vehicle on railroad tracks?
options: a:Never stop on the tracks.,b:If no trains are nearby.,c:Only when crossing and already partway across.
note: Never stop on railroad tracks. Do not begin to cross unless your vehicle can entirely clear the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed.,c:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed only when safe.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A no passing zone.,c:A speed limit regulation.
note: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are in a school zone or approaching a school crossing—exercise extra caution for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, in what order should you scan the intersection before proceeding?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Look right first, then left, then right again.,c:Only check your rearview mirror.
note: At a stop, look left first because vehicles from that side are closer; then check right, and left again before proceeding.

question: In winter driving conditions, how much longer should you allow for stopping distance compared to normal?
options: a:At least three times the normal stopping distance.,b:Twice the normal stopping distance.,c:Five times the normal stopping distance.
note: Snow and ice greatly increase stopping distance; allow at least three times the normal distance to stop safely.

question: If your wheels drop off the paved road onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and sharply turn back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: Reduce speed without braking hard, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when it is safe to do so to avoid losing control.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wearing your seat belt.,b:Limiting driving to weekdays.,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury in a crash.

question: A lack of sleep affects your driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of anger.
note: Fatigue impairs driving ability similar to alcohol. For example, staying awake 18 hours impairs driving comparably to about a 0.05% BAC.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train before crossing and ensure room to clear the tracks.,b:Always stop before crossing regardless of trains.,c:Cross as quickly as possible without checking for trains.
note: At crossings without gates or lights, slow and look both ways; never enter unless there is room to clear the track on the other side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes on an interstate?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot.,b:Always use cruise control before changing lanes.,c:Stop on the shoulder to check traffic.
note: Signal and check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes or passing on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal, adjust speed to match traffic, yield to existing freeway traffic, and merge when safe.,b:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Enter and drive slowly until you find open space.
note: When merging, match the speed of freeway traffic, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:You must not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down immediately.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the roadway mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:There is a pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is approaching.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction except to turn into a driveway or make a permitted left turn.

question: When a steady green arrow is displayed at an intersection, what does it permit drivers to do?
options: a:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.,c:Stop and wait for a green circle instead.
note: A steady green arrow allows you to turn in the arrow’s direction, but you must yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: When confronted with another driver's aggressive behavior, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and allow them to pass.,b:Retaliate by tailgating them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: Do not engage with aggressive drivers; create distance and let them pass to diffuse the situation.

question: What is illegal for a passenger in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Possessing an open container of alcohol.,b:Sleeping in the passenger seat.,c:Using a hands-free device.
note: It is unlawful for anyone to possess or drink from an open alcoholic container in a vehicle on a public road.

question: What is a driver's responsibility when interacting with pedestrians?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if they are wrong.,b:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to the right-of-way.,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of your vehicle before proceeding.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing where they should not be.

question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road; broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass.

question: Why should you be especially cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:Because the bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Because oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass and the bicyclist may swerve.
note: Bicyclists can be forced to swerve by obstacles and other roadway hazards; ensure there is room and that oncoming traffic is clear before passing.

question: Which conviction may result in losing your license as described in the handbook?
options: a:Passing a stopped school bus.,b:Failing to yield the right-of-way.,c:Driving without a license.
note: Certain offenses, such as passing a stopped school bus, can result in license suspension or loss if enough points accumulate.

question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe (treat it like a stop sign).,b:Drive through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left to prepare for the turn.,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you begin the turn.,c:Flash your headlights to signal drivers to yield.
note: Keep your front wheels straight while waiting to turn left; this prevents being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: If your license has been previously suspended and reinstated, how many points accumulated within three years will cause another suspension?
options: a:Eight points,b:Five points,c:Four points
note: Accumulating eight points within a three-year period against a previously suspended license will result in another suspension.

question: When it is raining, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain to improve visibility without causing glare for other road users.

question: When driving on major highways, you should:
options: a:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards.,b:Fix your gaze on the center of the road to avoid distractions.,c:Use cruise control at all times to reduce effort.
note: To avoid 'highway hypnosis' remain alert, scan the road, and be ready to respond to unexpected hazards.

question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is influenced by each of the following except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you consume.
note: BAC depends on the quantity consumed, the time over which it is consumed, and body weight. The type of alcoholic beverage does not determine BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A No Stopping sign means you may stop only for what reason?
options: a:To avoid a conflict with other traffic or to obey a traffic officer.,b:To unload packages momentarily.,c:To discharge passengers anywhere along the road.
note: No Stopping means stop only to obey a traffic control signal or officer or to avoid a conflict with traffic.

question: If you hear or see an emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are open.,c:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching, move out of its path and stop safely to allow it to pass; don't try to outrun it.

question: What is a primary effect of distracted driving?
options: a:It usually causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,b:It always makes drivers more alert.,c:It never affects driving ability.
note: Distractions generally delay a driver’s perception and reaction to road hazards, increasing crash risk.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol, certain medications, and lack of sleep.,b:Only alcohol.,c:Only illegal drugs.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness; good physical condition is essential for safe driving.

question: How long will your license be suspended for a first conviction of driving at 55 mph when that exceeds the speed limit by 15 mph or more?
options: a:30 days,b:One week,c:Two weeks
note: If you are driving at least 55 mph and exceed the speed limit by 15 mph or more, a first conviction results in at least a 30-day license suspension.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow because high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: If your license is suspended a third time due to the point system, how long is the suspension?
options: a:12 months.,b:10 months.,c:10 weeks.
note: In North Carolina, a third suspension under the point system results in a 12-month license suspension.

question: What does an orange traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A school zone ahead.,b:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,c:A railroad crossing ahead.
note: Orange signs are used to warn drivers of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations in or near the roadway.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, which steps should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,c:Drive around lowered gates if traffic is heavy.
note: At railroad crossings, look and listen for trains, obey signals and gates, and stop if lights are flashing or gates are down.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced and your field of vision is smaller.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night narrows your usable field of vision, making it harder to detect hazards in time to stop.

question: How many points on your license may result in assignment to a driver improvement clinic?
options: a:Seven points.,b:Five points.,c:Three points.
note: If you accumulate seven license points in North Carolina, you may be assigned to a driver improvement clinic; the fee is currently $65.

question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign—you must stop.,b:The signal is malfunctioning and can be ignored.,c:You may slow down but not stop.
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop; then proceed only when the way is clear.
